verdict.rationale: Zapier documents its own headless execution paths. The SDK is installed via npm, authenticates with client credentials and executes actions across apps. The SDK CLI runs actions directly from the terminal, and stored actions can be executed by id through an API call. However, nothing explicitly documents CI pipeline usage or non-interactive auth for the CLI, so the CI part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD integration docs or examples, documented non-interactive/token-based auth for the SDK CLI in pipelines, independent hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Install @zapier/zapier-sdk via npm, authenticate with OAuth or client credentials, and execute actions across 9,000+ apps.
The Zapier SDK CLI lets you explore and run actions across {appCount} apps directly from your terminal, authenticated, with no OAuth setup required.
Creates a new stored action entry that can then be executed from a simpler call to /stored-actions with just the stored action `id`.
